question: P and Q start from point A to point B, at the same time at speeds of 32 km/h and 40 km/h, respectively. If in covering the journey P takes 15 minutes longer than Q, the total distance AB of the journey is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio of P : Q = 32 : 40 = 4 : 5

Time ratio of P : Q = 5 : 4 (since Distance is constant)

Difference in time ratio = 5 − 4 = 1 unit → 15 minutes

Actual time taken by Q = 4 units → 4 × 15 = 60 minutes = 1 hour

Total Distance = Speed of Q × Time taken by Q = 40 × 1 = 40 km

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of P = 32 km/h

Speed of Q = 40 km/h

Difference in time taken = 15 minutes = 15/60 hours = 1/4 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
• 
 
 
 A
 
 
 B
 
 Distance = D km
 
 
• 
 

 P : 32 km/h
 (takes 15 min more)

 
• 
 

 Q : 40 km/h

**Calculations:**

Let the total distance be D km.

⇒ Time taken by P = D/32

⇒ Time taken by Q = D/40

⇒ (D/32) − (D/40) = 1/4

⇒ (5D − 4D) / 160 = 1/4

⇒ D/160 = 1/4

⇒ D = 160 ÷ 4

⇒ D = 40 km

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Formula for Distance

If two speeds are S₁ and S₂ and the absolute time difference is Δt, then Distance = [(S₁ × S₂) ÷ |S₁ − S₂|] × Δt.

Average Speed

If a certain distance is covered at speed x and the same distance is covered at speed y, then the Average Speed for the entire journey = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. In opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
